title: Laboratory apparatus and instruments
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Integrated Science; not yet checked by a CBC Integrated Science teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Real apparatus on a tray: a beaker, a measuring cylinder, a test tube and holder, a thermometer, a metre rule, a balance and a stopwatch (or a phone timer). The child reads a measuring cylinder at eye level at the bottom of the curve. Bunsen burners and spirit lamps are lit only by the teacher.

skills.key_step: The child names and uses the science skills in order (observe, measure, classify, predict, test, record, communicate, conclude) and keeps a prediction apart from a result and a conclusion.

floor.prerequisite: Has predicted and tested in Grade 5 (floating and sinking).
floor.question: Does a plasticine boat float?

representations: a floating test repeated with several objects
steps: Observe with all safe senses and instruments.
Conclude from several results; communicate in a table or chart.
contexts: testing which soil holds most water

board.do: Write "Prediction" and "Result" as two headings.
Write "the stone will float" under Prediction.
Point at Result.
board.say: What goes here, and when is it written?

board.do: Wait for "what happened, after the test".
Ask the child to write a conclusion from three results.

misconceptions.ask: When do we write the prediction: before or after?
misconceptions.repair: A prediction comes before the test; the result after.

misconceptions.ask: How can you observe a sound or a smell safely?
misconceptions.repair: Observing uses all safe senses and instruments.

misconceptions.ask: Is a conclusion made before or after the results?
misconceptions.repair: A conclusion comes from the results.

checks.question: What is the difference between a prediction and a result?
checks.answer: a prediction is said before the test; a result is what happened

checks.question: Why should a test be repeated?
checks.answer: to make sure the result is reliable before concluding

skills.key_step: The child says what common apparatus is for, uses it correctly (measuring cylinder at eye level at the bottom of the curve, thermometer read in the liquid, balance zeroed) and looks after it.

floor.prerequisite: Can measure in litres and kilograms.
floor.question: How many millilitres are in one litre?

representations: a drawing of the meniscus at eye level
steps: Name the apparatus and its job.
Use it the right way (eye level, bulb in liquid, zero the balance).
Report broken glass to the teacher.

board.do: Draw a measuring cylinder with a curved water surface.
Draw an eye level with the curve.
Point at the curve.
board.say: Do we read at the top or the bottom of the curve?

board.do: Wait for "the bottom".
Mark the reading at the bottom of the curve.

misconceptions.ask: Which has finer marks: the beaker or the cylinder?
misconceptions.repair: Use a measuring cylinder for exact volumes.

listen_for: read the top of the curve
misconceptions.repair: Read at eye level at the bottom of the curve.

misconceptions.ask: Which flame is used for heating: blue or yellow?
misconceptions.repair: The blue flame (air hole open) is the hottest.

misconceptions.ask: What happened to the reading in the air?
misconceptions.repair: Read the thermometer in the liquid.

checks.question: Which apparatus measures the volume of a liquid most exactly: a beaker or a measuring cylinder?
Where do you read the level of water in a measuring cylinder?
checks.answer: at eye level, at the bottom of the curve

skills.key_step: The child gives the SI unit of each basic quantity: length (metre), mass (kilogram), time (second), temperature (kelvin), electric current (ampere), and keeps mass apart from weight.

floor.prerequisite: Knows the metre and the centimetre.
floor.question: How many centimetres are in a metre?

representations: a chart of quantities and units
a metre rule, a 1 kg bag of sugar, a stopwatch
steps: Mass: kilogram (kg); weight is a force, in newtons.
contexts: a phone charger label in amperes

board.do: Draw a table: quantity, SI unit, symbol.
Fill in length.
Point at the mass row.
board.say: Is the SI unit the gram or the kilogram?

board.do: Wait for "the kilogram".
Ask the child to fill in the other rows.

misconceptions.ask: Which unit is on a packet of sugar: 1 kg or 1,000 g? Which is the SI unit?
misconceptions.repair: The SI unit of mass is the kilogram.

misconceptions.ask: Is weight a pull of gravity (a force)?
misconceptions.repair: Mass is in kilograms; weight, a force, is in newtons.

misconceptions.ask: What unit do scientists use for temperature in SI?
misconceptions.repair: The SI unit of temperature is the kelvin.

misconceptions.ask: Which is the smallest of second, minute, hour?
misconceptions.repair: The SI unit of time is the second.

checks.question: What is the SI unit of length?
What is the SI unit of electric current?

skills.key_step: The child builds derived units from base units: area (m²), volume (m³), speed (m/s), density (kg/m³), by following the formula.

floor.question: What is the SI unit of time?

representations: a square metre marked on the floor
steps: Write the formula (area = length x width).
Put units in place of the quantities (m x m).
Check: speed = distance / time gives m/s.
contexts: the area of a classroom floor
the volume of a water tank

board.do: Write "speed = distance / time".
Ask what the unit of speed will be.
Wait for "m/s".
Write "density = mass / volume".
Ask the child to build the unit of density.

misconceptions.ask: What is the SI unit of length? What is length cubed?
misconceptions.repair: The SI unit of volume is the cubic metre.
Speed is in metres per second.

misconceptions.ask: What is divided by what in density?

checks.question: What is the SI unit of area?
What is the SI unit of speed?
